beats: In 897, a man was put on trial nine months after he died!
His body was dug up, dressed in his old robes, and propped on a throne.
The judge was Pope Stephen the Sixth. The defendant was a former pope, Formosus.
A deacon stood beside the corpse to answer for him.
Stephen hurled accusations. The corpse stayed silent.
They ripped off his robes, cut off his blessing fingers, and threw his body into the Tiber.
Then an earthquake cracked the very church where the trial was held!
Rome was disgusted. Rumors spread that the body had washed ashore and was working miracles.
Within months, Stephen was overthrown, thrown in prison, and strangled!
The next popes cancelled the verdict and reburied Formosus in St. Peter's, in full papal robes.
Legend says the saints' images bowed to him as he passed.
Case closed. Until one of the original judges became pope, and declared him guilty all over again!
